definitions.explanation: Sake served chilled, typically refrigerated rather than at room temperature. Many premium sakes are best enjoyed cold to bring out subtle flavors.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{冷酒|れいしゅ}がおいしい。
examples.english: Cold sake tastes great in summer.

examples.japanese: {冷酒|れいしゅ}を{一杯|いっぱい}ください。
examples.english: One glass of cold sake, please.

examples.japanese: {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}は{冷酒|れいしゅ}で{飲|の}むと{香|かお}りがよくわかる。
examples.english: When you drink ginjo sake chilled, you can really appreciate its aroma.

notes:
Compound of {冷|れい} (cold) + {酒|しゅ} (sake). Refers specifically to sake served cold, in contrast to {熱燗|あつかん} (hot sake) or {常温|じょうおん} (room temperature).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷酒|れいしゅ}を{頼|たの}む: to order cold sake
- {冷|ひ}えた{冷酒|れいしゅ}: well-chilled sake
- {冷酒|れいしゅ}グラス: cold sake glass

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {熱燗|あつかん}: hot sake (warmed)
- {常温|じょうおん}: room temperature (sake)
- {日本酒|にほんしゅ}: sake (general term)
- {冷|ひ}や: cold/cool — older term, sometimes refers to room-temperature sake in traditional contexts
